APT
Advanced Persistent Threat. A skilled, patient, usually government-backed hacking group.
ASN
Autonomous System Number. The ID of a network that owns a block of IP addresses, for example AS2856 (BT).
ATT&CK
MITRE's free catalogue of attacker tactics and techniques, each with an ID such as T1566.
BEC
Business Email Compromise. Fraud where attackers use or fake a real business email account to redirect payments.
C2
Command and Control. The server an attacker uses to send orders to infected machines.
CAF
Cyber Assessment Framework. NCSC's framework for assessing organisations running essential services.
CNI
Critical National Infrastructure. Services the country depends on, like energy, water and health.
CPE
Common Platform Enumeration. A standard name for a product, used to match vulnerabilities to software.
CVE
Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures. A unique ID for a publicly known security bug, for example CVE-2024-3400.
CVSS
Common Vulnerability Scoring System. Rates how severe a bug is, from 0 to 10.
Defanging
Changing an indicator so it cannot be clicked by accident, for example evil[.]com or hxxp://.
EDR
Endpoint Detection and Response. Security software on laptops and servers that watches for attacker behaviour.
Enrichment
Adding context to raw data (owner, location, reputation, history) so people can decide what to do.
EPSS
Exploit Prediction Scoring System. The estimated chance (0-1) a CVE is exploited in the next 30 days.
Exfiltration
Stealing data by copying it out of a network.
Hash
A fingerprint of a file, such as SHA-256. Change one byte and the hash changes completely.
IOA
Indicator of Attack. Behaviour showing an attack in progress.
IOC
Indicator of Compromise. A clue that something bad happened: a hash, IP, domain or URL.
Initial access
The first foothold an attacker gets inside a network, for example through phishing or a vulnerable VPN.
Infostealer
Malware that steals saved passwords, cookies and session tokens from a computer.
KEV
CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue: bugs confirmed to be used in real attacks.
Lateral movement
An attacker moving from the first machine they took over to other machines in the network.
Leak site
A website where ransomware gangs name victims and publish stolen data to pressure them into paying.
MFA
Multi-Factor Authentication. Proving who you are with more than a password, such as an app prompt.
MISP
Free, open source platform for storing, enriching and sharing threat intel.
Passive DNS
A historical record of which domains pointed to which IP addresses over time.
Phishing
Tricking people with fake messages into giving up passwords, money or access.
PIR
Priority Intelligence Requirement. One of the key questions a client needs answered.
Pivot
Using one indicator to discover related ones, for example from a domain to its IP to other domains.
Ransomware
Malware that encrypts or steals data and demands payment.
RaaS
Ransomware as a Service. Gangs rent their ransomware to 'affiliates' who carry out attacks for a cut.
SIC code
Standard Industrial Classification. The UK code describing what business a company does.
SIEM
Security Information and Event Management. A system that collects logs and raises alerts.
STIX
Structured Threat Information eXpression. A standard JSON format for sharing threat intel.
TAXII
The protocol used to send and receive STIX data over the internet.
TLP
Traffic Light Protocol. Labels (CLEAR, GREEN, AMBER, AMBER+STRICT, RED) that set who may see shared info.
TTP
Tactics, Techniques and Procedures. How an attacker behaves.
Typosquatting
Registering lookalike domains to trick people, for example paypa1.com.
Zero-day
A vulnerability attackers use before the vendor has released a fix.
Admiralty Code
A grading system for intel: source reliability (A-F) plus information credibility (1-6).
